newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: BOTSWANA NEEDS ACTIVE SECONDARY MARKET - C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: BOTSWANA NEEDS ACTIVE SECONDARY MARKET - C.BANK.

text.p: Botswana needs to develop an active secondary capital market to help boost access to finance, the Bank of Botswana said in its annual economic review for 1966.

The central bank highlighted the lack of commercial credit and finance to small and medium scale enterprises and said the objectives of Botswana's National Development Plan 8 (NDP8), which will run from the end of 1997 for five years, would be furthered by a more efficient and deeper financial sector.
"Effort is needed to develop an active secondary market for money and capital market instruments," the Bank said.
"The financial sector is not channelling resources to private sector investment projects to the extent necessary for significant economic diversification."
"The financial system has grown along with the economy, but has not increased its role," the Bank says.

To finance smaller enterprises, the Bank suggests the formation of a "second-tier" on the Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE), a Venture Capital Company (VCC) and an indigenous bank to compete with the four foreign-owned operators, who should reassess their risk criteria and change their attitudes.
"A 'second tier' market on the BSE could encourage smaller, newer firms - which do not meet the profitability and track record requirements for a normal listing - to raise funds," the Bank says.
"An alternative is the establishment of a venture capital company to seek out and fund new, risky, but promising, businesses."
The VCC could itself be listed on the BSE, thus providing indirect access for firms to the equity market.

The Bank added that although government would not need to borrow during NDP 8, it could introduce measures to develop the debt market, through issues of government securities, such as Treasury Bills or Government Bonds.
Lending to parastatals accounted for 2,750 million out of a total of 5,200 million pula oustanding loans and advances as at the end of 1996.

The securitising of these loans - selling the rights to the flow of interest and capital payments - would bear the characteristics of a long term bond which could be marketable, and be quoted and traded on the BSE.
It was likely that a bond issue by Botswana Teleocmmunications would be made in 1997 and it was hoped more parastatals would be in a position to raise funds in this way during NDP8.
